dateline: New Delhi / Islamabad / Gilgit-Baltistan / Srinagar / United Nations — August 1947–Present
heroHeadline: Day 393: Pakistan Holds GB Assembly Elections Defying India Sovereignty Protest; India Rejects Kashmir Claims at UNGA — Ceasefire at Day 393, Bilateral Freeze Comprehensive
heroSubtitle: June 7, 2026: Pakistan proceeded with elections for 24 Gilgit-Baltistan Assembly seats (396 candidates, 958,480 voters) despite India's June 5 formal sovereignty protest declaring GB is 'an integral and inalienable part of India illegally occupied by Pakistan.' Preliminary results show PPP leading in Gilgit constituency; Pakistan's Foreign Office dismissed India's protest as 'fake narratives.' On June 6, India's UN envoy Parvathaneni Harish rebutted Pakistan's Kashmir claims at UNGA: 'J&K was, is, and will always remain an integral part of India' — accusing Pakistan of a 'carefully choreographed attempt to conflate fact with fiction.' Pakistan's Political Coordinator at the UN demanded a UN-supervised plebiscite. The ceasefire holds at Day 393 with no LOC violations since May 10, 2025. Bilateral freeze comprehensive: no ambassadors, $0 formal trade, IWT 'in abeyance' with India's PCA award rejection operative, Pakistan airspace ban through June 23-24, four back-channel contacts the only bilateral interaction. Post-Sindoor arms race accelerates: Pakistan Fatah-4 cruise missile (750km) operational; both sides planning ~14% defense budget increases for 2026-27 with no arms control framework in place.
footerNote: Data sourced from Indian MEA/MOD, Pakistan ISPR/MFA, UN Security Council, SIPRI, Crisis Group, HRW, Stimson Center
